diagnosis: Calculation of number needed to treat
mechanism: Number needed to treat is the reciprocal of the absolute risk reduction: NNT = 1 / (control event rate − treatment event rate), conventionally rounded up to the next whole patient when needed.
vignette: In a randomized trial, the outcome occurs in 20% of participants receiving standard care and in 10% of participants receiving a new treatment over the same follow-up interval.
lead: What is the number needed to treat to prevent one additional outcome?
distractor_notes: An NNT of 2 would correspond to an absolute risk reduction of 50%, not 10 percentage points.
An NNT of 5 would correspond to an absolute risk reduction of 20%.
An NNT of 20 would correspond to an absolute risk reduction of 5%.
An NNT of 50 would correspond to an absolute risk reduction of 2%.
key_expl: The absolute risk reduction is 0.20 − 0.10 = 0.10. Number needed to treat is the reciprocal of the absolute risk reduction: 1 / 0.10 = 10. Thus, 10 patients must receive the new treatment over the stated interval to prevent one additional outcome compared with standard care.
objective: Calculate NNT as the reciprocal of absolute risk reduction.
